messages:
jun: FYI — noticed a p99 +12% regression on qwen2.5 text-gen after yesterday's autokernel switch. Happens on hosted clusters serving multilang traffic. Repro with our perf harness on a small sample.
jun: baseline (yesterday): 98ms p50 / 320ms p99; after change: 105ms p50 / 358ms p99. CPU/GPU usage looks the same.
perf-bot: automated profile: https://perf.redwood.local/graph/1726001111 (flamegraph + allocation heatmap). Key hotspot: kernel_selector::choose() spending ~45ms more on certain sequences.
nana: @jun can you post a short trace from the runtime with kernel hints and batch sizes? wondering if selector is thrashing between kernels for short vs long sequences.
jun: posted snippet from runtime trace: ```[1726001111] request id=aa12 seq_len=34 kernel_hint=auto selected=fast_mm candidate=fast_gemm latency_ms=14 selected_cost_est=1.1 alt_cost_est=1.05``` and another: ```[1726001112] request id=aa13 seq_len=280 kernel_hint=auto selected=fast_gemm candidate=autokernel_mm latency_ms=62 selected_cost_est=3.2 alt_cost_est=2.95```
kevin: seems selector is picking a slightly cheaper kernel for long seqs but runtime switch/launch overhead wins back for medium lengths. I bet batching heuristics + kernel launch jitter cause the p99 tail.
maria: also saw odd kv-cache invalidations correlated with multilingual tokenization. If tokenizer splits same logical token differently in CJK+latin sequences, the KV key entropy changes and cache hit rate drops — increases end-to-end work.
nana: example tokenizer split we saw: ```input: "你好, world" tokens: ["你","好",","," world"] vs expected ["你","好",",","world"] (leading space included)``` That space leads to different token lengths and affects continuous batching grouping.
kevin: quick experiment idea: pin kernel for qwen2.5 to the pre-autokernel choice for canary traffic and measure p99 delta. Command: ```rdw_exec --model qwen2.5 --kernel override:fast_gemm --route canary-5pct --metrics tags=kernel_override```
jun: ran that against canary (5%) for 10m: p99 dropped back ~6% vs current deploy but still +4% vs yesterday baseline. So kernel override helps but doesn't fully fix.
perf-bot: profiling diff (canary vs current): top deltas 
  kernel_switch_overhead +34ms
  kv_cache_miss_work +18ms
  batch_scheduler_wait +12ms

maria: sounds like three orthogonal issues: kernel launch overhead for borderline seq lengths, kv cache miss from tokenizer edgecases, and our batch sampler producing uneven groups for multilang mixes.
nana: prioritized action items: 1) add tokenizer normalization pass that strips stray leading spaces in CJK-Latin adjacency (low risk), 2) tweak batch sampler to shard on tokenized-length-buckets + language tag, 3) temporary kernel override for qwen2.5 while we tune selector heuristics.
kevin: for selector heuristics we should add a tiny correction term: penalize kernel_switch_count per second per worker to prefer stable kernel across batch, e.g. in pseudocode: ```score = perf_estimate - alpha * recent_switches``` where alpha tuned from 0.2..1.0.
jun: implemented alpha=0.5 in a local build and ran perf harness: p99 improved -5% relative to current. I'll push PR tomorrow with metrics and tests.
ops-bot: deploy bot: canary rollout initiated by jun: qwen2.5-autokernel-alpha=0.5 -> canary 5% at 1726001120.
maria: small config snippet for batch sampler to try: ```{
  "sampler": "latency_aware",
  "buckets": [32,64,128,256,512],
  "max_batch_ms": 12,
  "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
  "language_shard": true
}```
kevin: also watch KV cache metrics: kv.hit_rate and kv.evictions/sec per model-version. If tokenizer patch improves hit_rate we should see >3% absolute lift.
jun: quick log showing kv misses for affected trace: ```kv_lookup key=0x7f12a3 miss true reason=token_split_mismatch seq=78```
nana: can we add a fuzz test to tokenizers CI that constructs CJK+latin adjacency cases and ensures no leading-space tokens get introduced? low friction and prevents regression.
jun: will add fuzz test + add normalization pass. will also run long-run canary with kernel override for 1h and post results.
ops-bot: canary status update: 5% -> healthy for 10m, no error rate uptick.
jun: final note: seems like the regression was not a single root cause — kernel selector micro-oscillation + tokenizer-induced kv churn + batching imbalance all stacked. plan: immediate tokenizer fix + sampler tweak + short-term kernel override; medium-term: selector penalty and better cost-model (include launch overhead).
maria: ack. I'll file a follow-up ticket for postmortem and metrics dashboard (kv.hit_rate, kernel_switches, batch_size_dist).
kevin: leaving two follow-up experiments: (A) run binary with kernel_override+sampler tweak, (B) run autokernel with selector-alpha=0.5. compare cost and p99.
jun: thanks — will coordinate and post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
